answer: One defence is a staking registry: an agent must lock a deposit in a public registry before it can trade, like a ship posting bond before entering a harbor. Peers mirror that registry and check the deposit is real before trusting any claim. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so the cost scales with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay once. Misbehaviour forfeits the bond, so fakes cost more than they can earn: quartz-clear economics that make the attack unprofitable.
